## Report: H. G. Wells, *The Time Machine*, chapters I–VI

**1. The question, frozen.** The title and the opening chapter both make one thing central: the Time Traveller's argument that "the geometry... taught you at school" is a misconception — Time is a fourth dimension, "there is no difference between Time and any of the three dimensions of Space except that our consciousness moves along it" — and so a machine can carry a man along it. The text answers other questions too (why the model vanished; why he returns in rags; why the future people are childlike). I test the central one: **Why did the model vanish, and what makes travel along Time possible?** Range: two Thursday evenings at Richmond. Kind of question: *what produces it*, forward from causes. Held still: his theory of the future, a later and unfinished question.

**2. The parts, in his own words.** P1 "any real body must have extension in four directions… Length, Breadth, Thickness, and—Duration"; P2 "Time is only a kind of Space"; P3 "a natural infirmity of the flesh"; P4 the portraits — "sections… of his Four-Dimensioned being, which is a fixed and unalterable thing"; P5 the barometer trace "along the Time-Dimension"; P6 the balloon against gravitation; P7 the machine and its two levers; P8 the Psychologist's "presentation below the threshold… diluted presentation"; P9 "slipping like a vapour through the interstices"; P10 his dust, cut chin, socks; P11 the narrator's "no kind of trick… could have been played upon us under these conditions".

**3. Part by part.**

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| P1 four directions | borrowed | rests on the school geometry; it is not tested here, and it states the conclusion inside a starting point |
| P2 Time is a kind of Space | loose | any weaker claim ("Time has a direction-like structure") licenses the same machine and the same story |
| P3 infirmity of the flesh | idle | remove it and every job is still done; it also absorbs any failure of sight, with no gauge |
| P4 portraits as sections | loose | photographs of the same man, or sections of a house, do the job as well. Held core: a series of snapshots is a series of slices |
| P5 barometer line | loose | a fever chart or a share price works as well. It shows we draw time on paper, not that we can travel it |
| P6 balloon | loose | a diving bell, a lift, a fish — all work. Held core: limits are practical, not absolute |
| P7 levers | held if | held only by the job "the model vanished by time travel", which is itself in doubt; what would settle it: a second vanish with the timing checked |
| P8 diluted presentation | loose | a catch-all with no gauge; it can absorb any failure of visibility, including the traveller's own visibility |
| P9 attenuation risk | loose | it said stopping should mean a far-reaching explosion; the stop brought him to soft turf and a cut chin, and the claim was never narrowed out loud |
| P10 his state | two routes | a real journey, or a hard night — the Journalist's "Amateur Cadger". Nothing on the change list separates them |

**4. Whole-explanation checks.** *Flip:* had the model stayed put, P1–P6 would stand exactly as written. So none of them does work for the vanish. *Reverse:* P8 runs backwards from the result — not seen, therefore diluted. That is fine for "what can we tell?" and not for "what produces it?". *Answer in the starting points:* P1 asserts the conclusion, so P2 is already inside it; P3 and P6 move the obstacle into us, where nothing can be looked at. *Pulls:* P4's "fixed and unalterable" against P2's "we are always getting away from the present moment… turn about and travel the other way" — if the whole is fixed, his journey is an inspection, not a trip, and the text never draws that line; P8's dimming against his own report of the sun leaping and the moon spinning — he should see less, not more; and he concedes "you cannot move at all in Time" three lines after saying consciousness moves along it. *Rivals:* the conjuring trick. The document hands us its track record — his own ghost last Christmas, the Tübingen sighting. P11 tries to kill it by observation conditions, but that kind of test can only ever look at the room, where a good trick succeeds. No change on the list tells the two apart: **at this level they are the same explanation**, and a finer question is owed. *Change list:* one entry — press the lever, it goes. What is left out is said out loud once, as a shrug: "Into the future or the past — I don't, for certain, know which." *Where the parts came from:* P1–P6, P8, P9 asserted; P7 built (two years' work, a stated behaviour it could have been caught out on); nothing fitted — he has met no cases. P10 is a reading, not the thing read.

**5. What would make it harder to vary.** (i) Send the model into the past by a stated amount, write down beforehand where it should be found, and go and look on the Thursdays before it was made. (ii) Give P8 a gauge: how slow would it have to run to be visible at one-fiftieth strength? Then run it that slowly.

**6. What this does not show.** Loose is not wrong. The geometry may be sound and the man may have travelled; nothing above rules it out. It says only that the story as told does not hold its parts in place.

**7. One next step.** Before pressing anything again, write both predictions down — where the model will be found, and what a slow run will look like — then run both.
